findings.title: HTTP client requests have no timeout
findings.description: http.DefaultClient has no timeout configured. Long-running network operations (e.g., hung TCP connection) will block the runner indefinitely, blocking the entire polling loop.
findings.scenario: If coordinator becomes unresponsive, runner goroutine hangs forever, never processes new jobs.
findings.impact: Critical for reliability. Runner can become unresponsive if coordinator has network issues.
findings.recommendation: Make timeout configurable via Config struct.

findings.title: No connection pooling or reuse optimization
findings.description: Each API call creates a new HTTP connection. Under high job load, this creates TCP connection churn.
findings.currentBehavior: Each call to fetchPendingJobs(), updateStatus(), postResult() uses default client which does maintain connection pool, but it's not optimized.
findings.fix: Create a custom http.Client with transport configuration in New() function.
findings.impact: Increased latency and resource usage under high load.

findings.title: No batching of job processing
findings.description: Each job is processed synchronously in sequence. If job execution is slow, it blocks polling for new jobs.
findings.consideration: Depends on use case - if job execution is slow, should process in parallel goroutines.
findings.fix: Consider processing jobs concurrently with goroutine pool or worker pattern.
findings.impact: If executor() is slow, job throughput is limited.
